subject: Note for those with accelerometer files holding more than 2 weeks of data

messages.author: 8d92e34685fbc6bd
messages.subject: Note for those with accelerometer files holding more than 2 weeks of data
parts:
Dear list,

Following up on the list activity last week I would like to explicitly highlight that there may have been problems with older versions of GGIR when applied to accelerometer files holding more than two weeks of data. Although, this is not a common scenario I think it is important bringing this to your attention.

This problem has been addressed in the current version 1.2-2, but will affect old analyses. The direct consequence of this bug would have been that you were not able to process a file or that the non-wear detection may not have worked.

As far as I can currently see this does not affect any of the published work relying on GGIR.

I would like to advise those who worked with older versions of GGIR (1.2-1 and earlier) on files with more than two weeks of data to either reprocess their data or at the very least review whether monitor non-wear time was detected in any of their files.

Kind regards,

Vincent
